### YMCA turns crisis into capability at scale

YMCA partnered with Accenture to build a community-based model that helps refugees and displaced
people gain skills, find work, and rebuild their futures—moving from relief to long-term capability.

[
Read more
][135]

### How UNICEF's GenU is closing the youth skills gap

Through UNICEF’s partnership with Accenture, young people gain access to AI-powered skilling,
digital learning and entrepreneurship opportunities that connect them to employment and brighter
futures.

[
Read more
][136]

### Philipstown's wire cars go global

Philipstown’s wire car tradition is accelerating onto the global stage through immersive
storytelling, gaming and commerce—fueling opportunity and driving impact far beyond the track.

[
Read more
][137]

### Google Cloud reimagines lead enrichment with agentic AI

The leading hyperscaler replaced batch processing with an agentic model that delivers decision-ready
outputs up to 30x faster—sharpening prioritization while enabling more confident sales decisions.

[
Read more
][138]

### Bristol Myers Squibb scales AI to rewire everyday work

The life sciences leader is putting people at the center of its AI ambition—rewiring work across the
enterprise to empower employees, drive innovation and accelerate the delivery of therapies to
patients.

[
Read more
][139]

## The trusted operator of the full enterprise AI stack, from governed private cloud to AI inference
## and agents in production.

From edge to core to cloud, we operate the infrastructure, data layer, and software integration to
deliver business outcomes with the predictable cost, reliability, security, and compliance that

## Recent News
1. Since July 2022, I work on building the Internet Computer at DFINITY.
2. Since June 2022, I have left AWS Lambda.
3. The paper co-authored at Amazon AWS with SeongJae Park on the topic of data-aware memory
   management in Linux was accepted at ACM HPDC (acceptance 19%).
   
4. Our paper, on the topic of [indexing in large-scale data processing systems][9] was accepted at
   IPDPS from the first reviewing round (10% acceptance ratio). The paper is in collaboration with
   Databricks, CWI, and TUDelft. Many thanks for the help.
   
5. Myself and our group in Leiden got featured in the [NWO I/O Magazine][10].
   
6. I have been awarded an **NWO VENI** grant on my project "Practical Performance Reproducibility in
   Cloud Systems Research" for €250,000, acceptance ratio ~12%.
   
7. Our paper on running [reproducible big data experiments in clouds][11] has been accepted and
   [presented][12] at NSDI in Feb 2020. Slides can be found [here][13]. Many thanks to the teams at
   U of Utah and UC Santa Cruz for the help.


## General Information

I am a senior researcher at DFINITY, building the Internet Computer.

Previously, I was an assistant professor at [LIACS, Leiden University][14], working in the Computer
Systems group and an Amazon Visiting Academic working with AWS Lambda.

I am a computer scientist with experience in both industry and academia, building large-scale
distributed systems and infrastructure. My focus is on empirical performance evaluation with a
strong emphasis on understanding, evaluating, and improving the performance of large-scale systems.
I am interested in and have experience with serverless platforms, data processing systems, general
distributed (storage) systems, and cloud computing. I have taught several courses on these topics
and trained and supervised students at all academic levels.

Previously, I was a postdoctoral researcher in the [Computer Systems Section][15] at the Department
of Computer Science of the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam in the [Massivizing Computer Systemsa Group,
led by prof.dr.ir. ][16][Alexandru Iosup][17].

In the summer of 2019, I was a research visitor in the [Flux Research Group][18] at the [University
of Utah][19], working closely with [dr. Robert Ricci][20].

In the summer of 2017, I worked as a research-intern at [Databricks][21], where I designed and
implemented a distributed index on Spark in collaboration with prof.dr. [Peter Boncz][22].

Previously, I briefly worked as a postdoctoral researcher under the supervision of prof.dr.ir.
[Henri Bal][23] on scalable IoT infrastructures.

In March 2017, I received my PhD from the Vrije Universiteit on [Optimizing the Execution of
Many-Task Computing Applications Using In-Memory Distributed File Systems"][24], under the
supervision of Dr.-Ing. habil. [Thilo Kielmann][25] and prof.dr.ir. [Henri Bal][26].

In 2012, I graduated my MSc with honors ("cum laudae") in high-performance distributed computing at
Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, with a thesis on [GPU-accelerated video encoding][27], under the
supervision of dr. Frank Seinstra.

I received my BSc diploma in 2009 in my home country, Romania, at the University of Bucharest,
Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science.

Please drop me a line if you want to collaborate or want to do a BSc or MSc project under my
supervision. For more information on the kind of projects I supervise, please see my [Projects][28]
or [Publications][29].

## Grants
1. **NWO VENI** - PI, Practical Performance Reproducibility in Cloud Systems Research -- €250,000.
   Project on studying how to achieve reproducible performance when running experiments in clouds.
   
   
2. **SURFsara, 2019-2020** - PI, DLPerf, Pilot Project for 500K Cartesius Cluster hours. Project on
   studying the performance bottlenecks of Deep-Learning Workloads.
   
3. **SURFsara, 2019** - PI, Granular Graph Processing, 50K compute hours for usage in the SURFsara
   HPCCloud; Project on assessing the impact of FaaS and Serverless paradigms on Graph Analytics.
   
4. **Google, 2018** - PI, Granular Graph Processing, $5,000 grant for usage in the Google Cloud.
   Project on assessing the impact of FaaS and Serverless paradigms on Graph Analytics.
   
5. **SURFsara, 2018** - PI, BDCloudVar, 70K compute hours in the SURFsara cloud. Project on studying
   the effects of performance variability on Big Da

## AMBROSYS

**Ambrosys **is a business consulting and IT services company. We provide infrastructure services,
professional consulting, HR services, outsourcing, and BPO solutions. Our team helps businesses
improve their operations with reliable technology and professional support. We also offer
**headhunting and recruitment services** to help organizations find the right candidates for their
needs. **Rajeswari**, Founder and Director of Ambrosys Business Solutions Pvt. Ltd., believes in
using smart systems to simplify business processes. Her vision is to reduce manual work through
automation so that professionals can focus more on innovation and growth.

# Welcome to Channel Dive

It’s a new day for tech channel news at Industry Dive and Informa TechTarget.

Published Oct. 30, 2025
[ [Phil Harvey's headshot] ][27]
[Phil Harvey][28] Editor-in-Chief

Pelicans fly over the Salton Sea at sunrise on July 7, 2011, in Salton City, California. David McNew
via Getty Images

Welcome to Channel Dive.

We're Informa TechTarget's new publication, focused on delivering daily news and analysis for
executives at North American channel partners — the diverse ecosystem of companies that resell,
deliver and add value to technology products and services. 

The [business combination][37] of [Industry Dive][38], the Informa Tech media brands, and TechTarget
provided us with the opportunity to assemble new teams and implement positive changes in our
approach to this market. 

We've sunset the [Channel Futures brand and website][39] and launched [Channel Dive][40] to provide
solid, dependable reporting to channel partners, while making it as easy as possible for them to
follow the topics that matter most. 

The seven newsletters previously sent by Channel Futures have been consolidated into a single [daily
newsletter][41], now available at Channel Dive. We aim to make the Channel Dive Daily as helpful and
uncluttered as possible. 

We took a similar approach with the Channel Dive website, featuring a highly functional and
minimalist design. We believe our audience will appreciate the absence of clickbait slideshows and
shouty headlines labeling every exec who changes jobs a "superstar." 

The [Channel Dive team][42] will feature reporting by Channel Futures alum James Anderson and Senior
Editor Matt Ashare, previously of CIO Dive, along with contributions from writers you've read before
on Channel Futures and other Industry Dive publications. The team will be managed by me, in addition
to my [daily editorial duties][43] at Light Reading.

Our goal is to earn your trust as a fair and valuable source of daily news and insights for channel
professionals. Let us know how we're doing and what issues you'd like us to cover next at
[[email protected]][44].

## FAQs

How do you improve AI cost efficiency?

Allocation, attribution, then optimization. The most effective levers are understanding where AI
spend is going, mapping it to the outcomes that drive the business, and optimizing their spend spend
based on what they learn. The CloudZero financial control plane provides full visibility on AI ROI.

What platforms can CloudZero connect to?

CloudZero can ingest and unify data from any AI, IaaS, PaaS, or SaaS provider. That includes
Anthropic, Open AI, Gemini, the big three, but also AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, Snowflake, Datadog,
MongoDB, and whatever else you’re using. We then convert the spend information into a common data
model and present it in a single pane of glass.

Can CloudZero show me a metric like cost per customer?

Yes. Our platform can calculate whatever unit cost metric is most important to you — including cost
per customer, per feature, per team, per transaction … the possibilities are endless.

Who is CloudZero for?

CloudZero is built for the teams that own the AI and cloud spend conversation. 

**Finance leaders (CFOs, FP&A, controllers) **tie every dollar of AI and cloud spend to the outcomes
they report on, such as customer, product, transaction, and P&L, so they can forecast it and defend
it to the board.

**Engineering leaders (CTOs, VPs of Engineering)** see what every model call, agent, and workload
costs in AI Hub and in their coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot), so they can pull
cost context where they already work, not chase it down after the bill arrives.

**Platform and cloud ops teams **author the allocation structure in CostFormation, so finance and
engineering see the same numbers, without months of tagging cleanup.

How long does it take to get started with CloudZero?

You can connect to the CloudZero platform in minutes and start seeing value right away. While some
special projects may require you to provide us with data, generally getting started requires very
little effort. From there, it only takes a few hours to uncover additional metrics like unit cost,
cost per customer, etc. Go [here][56] to review our entire setup process and the time commitment you
can expect at each step.

How much does CloudZero cost?

CloudZero uses a tiered pricing model that’s steady, predictable, and won’t vary month to month.
Unlike other cloud cost products, we don’t charge monthly overages — so, if your spend spikes one
month, your price stays the same.

## FAQs

How do you improve AI cost efficiency?

Allocation, attribution, then optimization. The most effective levers are understanding where AI
spend is going, mapping it to the outcomes that drive the business, and optimizing their spend spend
based on what they learn. The CloudZero financial control plane provides full visibility on AI ROI.

What platforms can CloudZero connect to?

CloudZero can ingest and unify data from any AI, IaaS, PaaS, or SaaS provider. That includes
Anthropic, Open AI, Gemini, the big three, but also AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, Snowflake, Datadog,
MongoDB, and whatever else you’re using. We then convert the spend information into a common data
model and present it in a single pane of glass.

Can CloudZero show me a metric like cost per customer?

Yes. Our platform can calculate whatever unit cost metric is most important to you — including cost
per customer, per feature, per team, per transaction … the possibilities are endless.

Who is CloudZero for?

CloudZero is built for the teams that own the AI and cloud spend conversation. 

**Finance leaders (CFOs, FP&A, controllers) **tie every dollar of AI and cloud spend to the outcomes
they report on, such as customer, product, transaction, and P&L, so they can forecast it and defend
it to the board.

**Engineering leaders (CTOs, VPs of Engineering)** see what every model call, agent, and workload
costs in AI Hub and in their coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot), so they can pull
cost context where they already work, not chase it down after the bill arrives.

**Platform and cloud ops teams **author the allocation structure in CostFormation, so finance and
engineering see the same numbers, without months of tagging cleanup.

How long does it take to get started with CloudZero?

You can connect to the CloudZero platform in minutes and start seeing value right away. While some
special projects may require you to provide us with data, generally getting started requires very
little effort. From there, it only takes a few hours to uncover additional metrics like unit cost,
cost per customer, etc. Go [here][56] to review our entire setup process and the time commitment you
can expect at each step.

How much does CloudZero cost?

CloudZero uses a tiered pricing model that’s steady, predictable, and won’t vary month to month.
Unlike other cloud cost products, we don’t charge monthly overages — so, if your spend spikes one
month, your price stays the same.

Our Process

## How We Build — and What You Can Expect

#### Discovery & Planning

Before writing a single line of code, we map your business goals, user flows, and technical
constraints — so the architecture decisions we make in week one don't become expensive rewrites in
month six.

You get a shared Jira board, a technical spec, and a realistic timeline. No vague estimates, no
scope surprises.

[Explore Our Discovery Process ][153]

#### Development & Testing

We work in two-week sprints with a live demo at the end of each. You see working software every
fortnight — not a finished product six months later that isn't what you pictured.

Unit tests, integration tests, and QA run in parallel with development. Bugs caught early cost a
fraction of what they cost post-launch.

[Explore Our Development Services ][154]

#### Deployment & Support

We deploy via CI/CD pipelines with automated rollback, zero-downtime releases, and health monitoring
from day one in production. No panic calls on launch night.

After launch we stay on — 24/7 monitoring, security patches, and performance tuning. Your product
doesn't stop evolving just because it shipped.

## Your Trusted Corporate Training Company for Global Instructor-Led Training

The rapid pace of digital and technological transformation is reshaping the way businesses operate,
making workforce upskilling not just important, but mission-critical. In a world where change is
constant, impactful and continuous learning has become a strategic priority. Instructor-led
training, especially in the post-COVID era, is proving to be one of the most effective ways to drive
real learning outcomes and build adaptable, future-ready teams.

Edstellar is your trusted partner in this transformation, a one-stop corporate training company
delivering scalable, high-quality instructor-led training across the globe. With a network of
10,000+ verified, certified trainers, we offer flexible, cost-effective on-site and virtual learning
solutions tailored to your organization’s goals. Our client-centric approach, global trainer
accessibility, and robust training management capabilities set us apart as a leading force in
corporate learning and development.

## What does Fastnexa do?

junior bench, and it starts from a measurable outcome agreed up front. Our teams work across the
United States, UAE, and Pakistan, so delivery keeps moving across time zones.

older systems. If you need a specific outcome, like a model in production, a SOC 2-ready pipeline, a

# Automation and Collaboration Workbench

GoInsight.AI unifies your teams, business systems, and AI into executable work that deliver real
results.

[Start Free Trial][34]

### More Than Just Chatbots

ChatGPT excels at ideation. GoInsight.AI extends that value into execution by connecting your
enterprise systems to automate end-to-end workflows, so decisions turn into actions instantly.

### Not Just a Workflow Builder

Tools like n8n shine in engineering-led automation. GoInsight.AI pairs robust automation with
business-ready delivery, so frontline teams can run it in one click, and leaders can track usage
anytime.

### Beyond a Closed Ecosystem

Most platforms try to lock you into their stack. GoInsight.AI brings your AI tools, automation, and
systems into the same workflow, enabling everything to be called and coordinated from one workbench.

## The Unified Hub for Enterprise AI and Automation

GoInsight.AI offers a multi-tiered strategy—automation drives everything within a compliant and
governed environment; AI is internalized as team capability; and a deeply integrated AI-automation
collaboration model empowers teams for continuous growth.

Track AI usage by team and process, including token spend and run metrics, to measure adoption depth

results.

[Start Free Trial][34]

### More Than Just Chatbots

ChatGPT excels at ideation. GoInsight.AI extends that value into execution by connecting your
enterprise systems to automate end-to-end workflows, so decisions turn into actions instantly.

### Not Just a Workflow Builder

Tools like n8n shine in engineering-led automation. GoInsight.AI pairs robust automation with
business-ready delivery, so frontline teams can run it in one click, and leaders can track usage
anytime.

### Beyond a Closed Ecosystem

Most platforms try to lock you into their stack. GoInsight.AI brings your AI tools, automation, and
systems into the same workflow, enabling everything to be called and coordinated from one workbench.

## The Unified Hub for Enterprise AI and Automation

GoInsight.AI offers a multi-tiered strategy—automation drives everything within a compliant and
governed environment; AI is internalized as team capability; and a deeply integrated AI-automation
collaboration model empowers teams for continuous growth.

Rapid Workflow Creation, No Code Required

Adapt Faster with Visual Workflow Orchestration

logic to create or update automations rapidly.

Connect Systems to Automate Work End-to-End

and more.

interact with native flows and AI apps on GoInsight.AI.
Controllable Automation, Measurable AI Value

Role-Based Access and Data Sharing Control

control over shared content to help protect corporate data boundaries.

and efficiency.

what data was used.

fully automated actions.

Transformation for every stage of growth

Enterprises

Startup Teams

Solo Developers
* Bridge Legacy & Cloud
  
  Connect systems that never talked to each other before - SaaS, internal tools, and data
  warehouses.

  Technical teams build complex workflows, while business users run them easily through
  GoInsight.AI's interface. AI solutions move beyond the tech team to frontline employees and
  everyday processes.
* Human + AI Operational Coordination
  
  Bring teams, workflows, and AI-powered operations into one coordinated environment where work can
  be executed, reviewed, and managed collaboratively across the enterprise.
* Enterprise-Grade Governance
  
  Provide fine-grained permissions, audit logs, and usage policies built-in, so your business
  activities in a controlled, IT-approved environment.
* Fast MVPs, Fast Iterations
  
  Build and test AI-powered products and workflows without having to wait for backend engineering.

  Link data and systems for lead routing, email workflows, CRM/database updates, reporting, and
  more.

  Even without coding, functional team members can trigger and interact with AI-driven workflows
  through a chat-based interface.
* All-in-One Toolkit
  
  Get the flexibility of code with the speed of no-code.
* Rapid Prototyping
  
  Spin up internal tools, workflows, and chatbots in minutes instead of days.

  Orchestrate APIs, databases, and AI models in one place.

GoInsight.AI is doing the work of at least 3 FTEs and, most importantly, is allowing us to be more
thorough in the work that we do.

Aaron Jewitt

Operation Director, AirDroid

GoInsight.AI gave us what we desperately needed: a single, secure environment to govern all our AI
initiatives. We went from fragmented, risky tools to a unified, compliant platform. It's not just an
automation tool; it's our central nervous system for enterprise AI.

Maria Chen

Chief Information Officer

We're not just automating tasks anymore; we are building a digital workforce. Our AI marketing
assistant now handles all our market research and campaign reporting. GoInsight.AI allowed us to
move beyond simple workflows and start creating intelligent, collaborative agents that learn and
grow with us.

Dr. Aris Thorne

Head of Innovation & Strategy

Before GoInsight.AI, our approval processes constantly stalled between systems, emails, and Slack
messages. Now we can automatically route requests, pause workflows for manager review, and resume
execution immediately after approval — without losing context or manually coordinating across teams.

Emily Carter

Director of Operations

Bring your team, systems, and AI into one place—then turn ideas into governed work.

## Built like a product team,
## Not an outsourcing vendor

Most companies don’t need an outsourcing vendor. They need an engineering team that understands
their product and stays invested in it.

That’s how we work. We embed with your team, learn your domain, and take ownership of the build —
architecture, development, testing, and release — so you’re not managing a task list, you’re
building a product with people who care how it turns out.

We’ve built real platforms in real estate, healthcare, education, and enterprise SaaS. Some from
zero. Some alongside existing teams. All of them running in production.

## How AI Fits Into How We Actually Build

AI is part of every serious engineering workflow now. We use it throughout the build: generating
boilerplate, writing tests, debugging, exploring architecture. Not to replace judgment. To remove
the friction that used to slow teams down.

In practice: more features per sprint, better test coverage, faster iteration. The engineers still
own every decision. AI handles the repetitive parts so they can focus on the harder ones.

We don’t exaggerate what it does. But we also won’t pretend it hasn’t changed how fast good software
gets built.

## What this means for your product:
* Faster prototypes, validated with working software not documents
* Better test coverage built in, not added before launch
* More engineering time on hard problems, less on repetitive ones
* Faster course-correction when the product needs to change direction

## The 2nd WORKSHOP ON HIGH PERFORMANCE SERVERLESS COMPUTING (2022)

Held in conjunction with [ACM HPDC 2022][6]
Minneapolis, Minnesota, United States. 30th June 2022

### WORKSHOP OVERVIEW

Serverless computing represents the next significant leap forward with respect to abstracting
commoditized computing resources. The main principle of serverless computing is that compute
providers deploy and manage the entire compute environment---from hardware through to runtime in
which an application executes; users therefore think entirely at the level of their application
without regard for the underlying computing environment. For example, the function as a service
(FaaS) model allows users to first register a programming function (e.g., in Python) and then they
may invoke that function many times with different input arguments.

Serverless computing is poised to become not only the face of cloud computing in the commercial
world, but also a model for remote and distributed computing more broadly. The workshop on High
Performance Serverless Computing will provide the high performance and distributed computing
community with a dedicated forum for discussing foundational research in serverless computing in
both industry and academia. The workshop will bring together these communities and provide a forum
for innovation in both the high performance and distributed systems that underlie serverless
computing platforms and also the use of serverless models for abstracting traditional high
performance and distributed computing systems.

### TOPICS

We invite the submission of original work that is related to the topics outlined below.
* Developing high performance serverless computing platforms
* Federation of serverless computing platforms
* Container management and scheduling
* Programming paradigms for serverless computing
* Data management for serverless computing
* Applications of serverless computing
* Benchmarking and performance of serverless computing
* On-demand and event-based computation
* Serverless economics and billing models
* Fault tolerance and reliability
* Data-intensive workloads and tools
* Productivity tools (Debugging, Profiling, Logging, etc)
* Stream and events processing
* Security in serverless
* Heterogeneous computing (GPU, Accelerators, exotic architectures)

### SUBMISSION

#### Important Dates
* Papers due: A̶p̶r̶i̶l̶ ̶8̶,̶ ̶2̶0̶2̶2̶ ̶A̶o̶E̶ ** April 15, 2021 AoE **
* Notifications: M̶a̶y̶ ̶0̶2̶,̶ ̶2̶0̶2̶2̶
* Camera ready: M̶a̶y̶ ̶0̶9̶,̶ ̶2̶0̶2̶2̶
* Workshop date: June 30, 2022

#### Paper Categories

Authors are invited to submit:
* Full 8-page papers
* Short/work-in-progress 4-page papers

#### Submission

Authors are invited to submit papers describing unpublished, original research. All submitted
manuscripts should be formatted using the ACM Master Template with sigconf format (please be sure to
use the current version). All necessary documentation can be found at:
[https://www.acm.org/publications/proceedings-template][7].

Papers may be either full (8 pages) or short (4 pages) including all text, figures, and references.
Papers will be peer-reviewed (single blind), and accepted papers will be published in the workshop
proceedings as part of the ACM Digital Library.

Papers conforming to these guidelines should be submitted through [EasyChair][8]

### ORGANIZATION

  ([foster@uchicago.edu][10])

# [High Performance Serverless][1]
* [Home][2]
* [Program][3]
* [Keynote][4]
* [Call For Papers][5]

## The 2nd WORKSHOP ON HIGH PERFORMANCE SERVERLESS COMPUTING (2022)

Held in conjunction with [ACM HPDC 2022][6]
Minneapolis, Minnesota, United States. 30th June 2022

### WORKSHOP OVERVIEW

Serverless computing represents the next significant leap forward with respect to abstracting
commoditized computing resources. The main principle of serverless computing is that compute
providers deploy and manage the entire compute environment---from hardware through to runtime in
which an application executes; users therefore think entirely at the level of their application
without regard for the underlying computing environment. For example, the function as a service
(FaaS) model allows users to first register a programming function (e.g., in Python) and then they
may invoke that function many times with different input arguments.

Serverless computing is poised to become not only the face of cloud computing in the commercial
world, but also a model for remote and distributed computing more broadly. The workshop on High
Performance Serverless Computing will provide the high performance and distributed computing
community with a dedicated forum for discussing foundational research in serverless computing in
both industry and academia. The workshop will bring together these communities and provide a forum
for innovation in both the high performance and distributed systems that underlie serverless
computing platforms and also the use of serverless models for abstracting traditional high
performance and distributed computing systems.

### TOPICS

We invite the submission of original work that is related to the topics outlined below.
* Developing high performance serverless computing platforms
* Federation of serverless computing platforms
* Container management and scheduling
* Programming paradigms for serverless computing
* Data management for serverless computing
* Applications of serverless computing
* Benchmarking and performance of serverless computing
* On-demand and event-based computation
* Serverless economics and billing models
* Fault tolerance and reliability
* Data-intensive workloads and tools
* Productivity tools (Debugging, Profiling, Logging, etc)
* Stream and events processing
* Security in serverless
* Heterogeneous computing (GPU, Accelerators, exotic architectures)

### SUBMISSION

#### Important Dates
* Papers due: A̶p̶r̶i̶l̶ ̶8̶,̶ ̶2̶0̶2̶2̶ ̶A̶o̶E̶ ** April 15, 2021 AoE **
* Notifications: M̶a̶y̶ ̶0̶2̶,̶ ̶2̶0̶2̶2̶
* Camera ready: M̶a̶y̶ ̶0̶9̶,̶ ̶2̶0̶2̶2̶
* Workshop date: June 30, 2022

#### Paper Categories

Authors are invited to submit:
* Full 8-page papers
* Short/work-in-progress 4-page papers

#### Submission

Authors are invited to submit papers describing unpublished, original research. All submitted
manuscripts should be formatted using the ACM Master Template with sigconf format (please be sure to
use the current version). All necessary documentation can be found at:
[https://www.acm.org/publications/proceedings-template][7].

Papers may be either full (8 pages) or short (4 pages) including all text, figures, and references.
Papers will be peer-reviewed (single blind), and accepted papers will be published in the workshop
proceedings as part of the ACM Digital Library.

Papers conforming to these guidelines should be submitted through [EasyChair][8]

### ORGANIZATION

Manuscripts submitted to The International Journal of Engineering Research & Technology should:
* contribute to existing research work;
* be original, and not have been published anywhere;
* present data clearly and concisely;
* mention engineering data & applications;

available on the IJERT Digital Library.

reviews are handled by state of art online manuscript review system, with a view towards making fast
& fair review process. The Editors reserve the right to reject papers without sending them out for
review.

range of branches of engineering and sciences. The major subject areas covered by the journal are

* Computer Science & Engineering
* Architecture and Planning
* Applied Sciences
* Applied Engineering
* Electronics & Communication Engineering
* Chemical Engineering
* Civil Engineering
* Textile Engineering
* Environmental Engineering
* Electrical Engineering
* Industrial Engineering
* Mechanical Engineering [**and more**][46]

There is **no any fee associated with submission to this journal.** We also offer discounts to
students and **100% fee waivers for researchers** in developing countries, determined using the
criteria* set by [WorldBank.][47]

Almost all university and colleges research in both science and engineering is performed as a
component of the advanced education of students. For most engineering & science students, the goal
of a career in industry motivates their pursuit of advanced study, and this will increasingly be the
case in the future and IJERT helps them to achieve their goal.

Software development is a young profession, and we are still learning the techniques and building
the tools to do it effectively. I've been involved in this activity for over three decades and in
the last two I've been writing on this website about patterns and practices that make it easier to
build useful software. The site began as a place to put my own writing, but I also use it to publish
articles by my colleagues.

In 2000, I joined [Thoughtworks][33], where my role is to learn about the techniques that we've
learned to deliver software for our clients, and pass these techniques on to the wider software
industry. As this site has developed into a respected platform on software development, I've edited
and published articles by my colleagues, both Thoughtworkers and others, to help useful writing
reach a wider audience.

[photo of Martin Fowler]

photo: Christopher Ferguson

Martin Fowler

# A website on building software effectively

If there's a theme that runs through my work and writing on this site, it's the interplay between
the shift towards agile thinking and the technical patterns and practices that make agile software
development practical. While specifics of technology change rapidly in our profession, fundamental
practices and patterns are more stable. So writing about these allows me to have articles on this
site that are several years old but still as relevant as when they were written.

As software becomes more critical to modern business, software needs to be able to react quickly to
changes, allowing new features to be conceived, developed and put into production rapidly. The
techniques of [agile software development][34] began in the 1990s and became steadily more popular
in the last decade. They focus on a flexible approach to planning, which allows software products to
change direction as the users' needs change and as product managers learn more about how to make
their users effective. While widely accepted now, agile approaches are not easy, requiring
significant skills for a team, but more importantly a culture of open collaboration both within the
team and with a team's partners.

This need to respond fluently to changes has an important impact upon the [architecture][35] of a
software system. The software needs to be built in such a way that it is able to adapt to unexpected
changes in features. One of the most important ways to do this is to write clear code, making it
easy to understand what the program is supposed to do. This code should be divided into modules
which allow developers to understand only the parts of the system they need to make a change. This
production code should be supported with automated tests that can detect any errors made when making
a change while providing examples of how internal structures are used. Large and complex software
efforts may find the [microservices][36] architectural style helps teams deploy software with less
entangling dependencies.

Creating software that has a good architecture isn't something that can be done first time. Like
good prose, it needs regular revisions as programmers learn more about what the product needs to do
and how best to design the product to achieve its goals. [Refactoring][37] is an essential technique
to allow a program to be changed safely. It consists of making small changes that don't alter the
observable behavior of the software. By combining lots of small changes, developers can revise the
software's structure supporting significant modifications that weren't planned when the system was
first conceived.

Software that runs only on a developer's machine isn't providing value to the customers of the
software. Traditionally releasing software has been a long and complicated process, one that hinders
the need to evolve software quickly. [Continuous Delivery][38] uses automation and collaborative
workflows to remove this bottleneck, allowing teams to release software as often as the customers
demand. For Continuous Delivery to be possible, we need to build in a solid foundation of
[Testing][39], with a range of automated tests that can give us confidence that our changes haven't
introduced any bugs. This leads us to integrate testing into programming, which can act to improve
our architecture.

## Data Management

There are many kinds of software out there, the kind I'm primarily engaged is Enterprise
Applications. One of the enduring problems we need to tackle in this world is [data management][40].
The aspects of data managment I've focused on here are how to migrate data stores as their
applications respond to changing needs, coping with different contexts across a large enterprise,
the role of NoSQL databases, and the broader issues of coping with data that is both Big and Messy.

## Domain-Specific Languages

A common problem in complex software systems is how to capture complicated domain logic in a way
that programmers can both easily manipulate and also easily communicate to domain experts.
[Domain-Specific Languages][41] (DSLs) create a custom language for a particular problem, either
with custom parsers or by conventions within a host language.

## Books

I've written seven books on software development, including Refactoring, Patterns of Enterprise
Application Architecture, and UML Distilled. I'm also the editor of a signature series for
Addison-Wesley that includes five jolt award winners.

[My Books Page...][42]

## Conference Talks


I'm often asked to give talks at conferences, from which I've inferred that I'm a pretty good
speaker - which is ironic since I really hate giving talks. You can form your own opinion of my
talks by watching videos of some my conference talks.

[My Videos Page...][43]

## Board Games


I've long been a fan of board games, I enjoy a game that fully occupies my mind, clearing out all
the serious thoughts for a bit, while enjoying the company of good friends. Modern board games saw
dramatic improvement in the 1990's with the rise of Eurogames, and I expect many people would be
surprised if they haven't tried any of this new generation. I also appear regularly on [Heavy
Cardboard][44].

[My Board Games page...][45]

## [The Archaeologist’s Copilot][173]

Thu 16 Jul 2026 09:25

When people think of legacy modernization, most folks aren't imagining the target environment will
be Java 8. But this was the challenge facing **Nik Malykhin** when he needed to run a Java 1.5
codebase on today's hardware. His early use of LLMs gave plausible answers that did not hold up in
the codebase. Progress came when he grounded the process in evidence, using AI to support analysis,
validation in a stable Docker environment, and gradual refactoring protected by tests. The main
takeaway is practical: AI was most useful when constrained by evidence, clear roles, and a
step-by-step modernization strategy.

[more…][174]

## [DSLs Enable Reliable Use of LLMs][175]

Tue 14 Jul 2026 08:51

LLMs generate code incredibly fast, but to ensure they generate exactly what is intended, they need
clear boundaries. Abstractions and Domain-Specific Languages (DSLs) provide a strong harness that
guides LLMs right from the start. **Unmesh Joshi** describes how the example of Tickloom - a domain
model and DSL for illustrating distributed system behavior - [shows how we can use an LLM][176] as a
partner to iteratively build a DSL and as a natural language interface to use it. Such a DSL can act
as the key source of truth for software systems in the world of LLMs.

techniques of [agile software development][34] began in the 1990s and became steadily more popular
in the last decade. They focus on a flexible approach to planning, which allows software products to
change direction as the users' needs change and as product managers learn more about how to make
their users effective. While widely accepted now, agile approaches are not easy, requiring
significant skills for a team, but more importantly a culture of open collaboration both within the
team and with a team's partners.

This need to respond fluently to changes has an important impact upon the [architecture][35] of a
software system. The software needs to be built in such a way that it is able to adapt to unexpected
changes in features. One of the most important ways to do this is to write clear code, making it
easy to understand what the program is supposed to do. This code should be divided into modules
which allow developers to understand only the parts of the system they need to make a change. This
production code should be supported with automated tests that can detect any errors made when making
a change while providing examples of how internal structures are used. Large and complex software
efforts may find the [microservices][36] architectural style helps teams deploy software with less
entangling dependencies.

Creating software that has a good architecture isn't something that can be done first time. Like
good prose, it needs regular revisions as programmers learn more about what the product needs to do
and how best to design the product to achieve its goals. [Refactoring][37] is an essential technique
to allow a program to be changed safely. It consists of making small changes that don't alter the
observable behavior of the software. By combining lots of small changes, developers can revise the
software's structure supporting significant modifications that weren't planned when the system was
first conceived.

Software that runs only on a developer's machine isn't providing value to the customers of the
software. Traditionally releasing software has been a long and complicated process, one that hinders
the need to evolve software quickly. [Continuous Delivery][38] uses automation and collaborative
workflows to remove this bottleneck, allowing teams to release software as often as the customers
demand. For Continuous Delivery to be possible, we need to build in a solid foundation of
[Testing][39], with a range of automated tests that can give us confidence that our changes haven't
introduced any bugs. This leads us to integrate testing into programming, which can act to improve
our architecture.

## Photostream

San Francisco

## Data Management

There are many kinds of software out there, the kind I'm primarily engaged is Enterprise
Applications. One of the enduring problems we need to tackle in this world is [data management][40].
The aspects of data managment I've focused on here are how to migrate data stores as their
applications respond to changing needs, coping with different contexts across a large enterprise,
the role of NoSQL databases, and the broader issues of coping with data that is both Big and Messy.

## Domain-Specific Languages

A common problem in complex software systems is how to capture complicated domain logic in a way
that programmers can both easily manipulate and also easily communicate to domain experts.
[Domain-Specific Languages][41] (DSLs) create a custom language for a particular problem, either
with custom parsers or by conventions within a host language.

## [The Archaeologist’s Copilot][173]

Thu 16 Jul 2026 09:25

When people think of legacy modernization, most folks aren't imagining the target environment will
be Java 8. But this was the challenge facing **Nik Malykhin** when he needed to run a Java 1.5
codebase on today's hardware. His early use of LLMs gave plausible answers that did not hold up in
the codebase. Progress came when he grounded the process in evidence, using AI to support analysis,
validation in a stable Docker environment, and gradual refactoring protected by tests. The main
takeaway is practical: AI was most useful when constrained by evidence, clear roles, and a
step-by-step modernization strategy.

[more…][174]

## [DSLs Enable Reliable Use of LLMs][175]

Tue 14 Jul 2026 08:51

LLMs generate code incredibly fast, but to ensure they generate exactly what is intended, they need
clear boundaries. Abstractions and Domain-Specific Languages (DSLs) provide a strong harness that
guides LLMs right from the start. **Unmesh Joshi** describes how the example of Tickloom - a domain
model and DSL for illustrating distributed system behavior - [shows how we can use an LLM][176] as a
partner to iteratively build a DSL and as a natural language interface to use it. Such a DSL can act
as the key source of truth for software systems in the world of LLMs.

Obligations is where we live.

**Our clients** are striving to meet accessibility compliance regulations and work diligently to
ensure their digital and physical environments are inclusive and usable for all individuals,
including those with disabilities.

**They focus on removing barriers and enhancing user experiences, aligning their services and
products with legal standards and ethical considerations to cater to a diverse and broader
audience.** This commitment reflects a dedication to social responsibility, legal compliance, and a

those with disabilities.

[Digital Accessibility Implementation Abstract Icon]

### Digital Accessibility Implementation

Implementing accessibility features into digital products to enhance usability for a diverse user
base.

[Accessibility Compliance Documentation Abstract Icon]

### Accessibility Compliance Documentation

Creating comprehensive documentation to demonstrate and maintain compliance with accessibility
standards.

Ensuring consistent accessibility across various platforms and devices for a seamless user
experience.

[Staff Augmentation Abstract Icon]

Specializing in creating websites that are fully accessible, following WCAG guidelines to ensure
usability for all users, including those with disabilities.

[Mobile Accessibility Development Abstract Icon]

### Mobile Accessibility Development

Developing mobile applications with accessibility in mind, ensuring they are usable by people with
various disabilities and comply with accessibility standards.

[Accessible E-commerce Solutions Abstract Icon]

### Accessible E-commerce Solutions

Crafting online shopping platforms that are accessible to all users, incorporating features that
enhance usability for people with disabilities.

[Accessibility Auditing and Remediation Abstract Icon]

### Accessibility Auditing and Remediation

### Accessible Content Management Systems (CMS)

Implementing CMS platforms that are accessible, allowing content creators to easily produce and
manage accessible content.

[Get your encrypted email][174]

defends freedom and puts people first.

Our transparency, open-source software, and rigorous encryption have earned Proton millions of users
— and the recommendation of the United Nations.

Tech companies like Google or Apple define privacy as “nobody can exploit your data, except for us.”
We believe nobody should exploit your data, period.

Our technology and business are based upon this fundamentally stronger definition of privacy, backed
also by Swiss privacy laws.

### Privacy for a better world

At Proton, we believe that a better world begins with privacy, and this is at the heart of
everything we do. Privacy isn’t just something we talk about; it’s a core belief and the reason
Proton was created in the first place.

We also believe in people before profits, and our primary shareholder is the nonprofit [Proton
Foundation][175], whose mission is to fight for an open internet that promotes freedom of speech and
freedom of information.

[Learn about our impact][176]

[Join Proton][177][Proton for Business][178]

Our end-to-end encryption and zero-access encryption mean that no one (not even Proton) has the
technical means to access your data without your permission.

We don’t sell ads and can’t share your data. At Proton, privacy isn’t a promise, it’s mathematically
ensured.

[Discover Proton’s encryption
][179]

### Swiss privacy

Proton is based in Switzerland, and your data does not go to the cloud. Instead, it stays under the
protection of some of the world’s strongest privacy laws.

We are a neutral and safe haven for your personal data, committed to defending your freedom.

[About Swiss privacy
][180]

Proton’s services are so simple and intuitive that anyone can use them. Move your emails, contacts,
and calendars from Google, Outlook, and other providers to Proton in just a few clicks.

Connect your Gmail to Proton Mail to read, send and receive your emails in one place, bringing you
one step closer to leaving behind Big Tech for good.

[Connect your Gmail account
][181]

Since we were founded by scientists, we know that trust is earned through transparency and peer
review.

All our apps are open source and independently audited by security experts so that anyone can
inspect them, use them, and trust them.

[Proton and open source
][182]

### One account, any device

Access your email, files, calendars, passwords, and VPN anywhere.

Get Proton apps on all your devices (Android, iPhone and iPad, Windows, macOS, Linux, and more) with

[See all Proton services
][183]

Privacy is a human right, so our services are always available for free, and our encryption tech is

# Hi, I’m Paul Swail.

## I guide small teams building serverless apps on AWS.

## New to Serverless?

If you’ve heard a lot about serverless but not sure about how to get started with it, my free
Transition to Serverless email course is a great place to start. It’s a 5-day course to teach you
both the why and how of adopting a serverless-first approach to building applications on AWS. You
can jump in here:

[Transition to Serverless »
Free Course][7]

## Popular Articles

I write regularly about serverless. Here’s a list of my most popular articles:

### Strategy & Engineering Approach
* [Beware “Best Practice”][8]
* [Paradigm shifts][9]
* [Optimising for the right thing at the right time][10]
* [The serverless value proposition for development agencies][11]
* [Infrastructure-as-Code is the linchpin practice for successful serverless teams][12]
* [The testing trade-off triangle][13]
* [Integration and E2E tests are the primary confidence drivers for serverless apps][14]

### Technical/How-tos
* [Comparing multi and single table approaches to designing a DynamoDB data model][15]
* [How to build a serverless photo upload service with API Gateway][16]
* [7 ways to do async message processing in AWS][17]
* [The Simple Guide to Testing within your Serverless CI/CD Pipelines][18]
* [Migrating a Monolithic SaaS App to Serverless — A Decision Journal (6-part series)][19]
